tei:div.tei:p:
Our God and the God of our fathers. When a certain manHaman. rose against us, fear and trembling took hold upon us; when he was associated with a king fond of adulation, we had well nigh succumbed. They determined to sell us, who were without any stay, like a heap of sand to fill up a moat; they said, “Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” Then our eyes were raised towards heaven, and we called upon thee to accurse such enemies, to cut off their name, and blot out their memory, and to extirpate them, to let my adversaries suffer for their malice, and let them be caught in the wiles which they deceitfully devised, saying, “The Lord shall not see it, neither shall the God of Jacob regard it.” But we reply, Though he afflict the scattered, and grieve them, yet he is not willing to consume them. For their former secret sins the Lord chastised them, making the kingAhasuerus. take off his signet, to terrify them, though it was only in appearance. For he performed his kind promise to exalt them in the eyes of the nations, and did not cast them away or abhor them to destroy them utterly in the land of their enemies. A hint of these events was given to the numerous and dispersed people in Deuteronomy,See Deut. xxxi. 18. the word Hester there referring to Esther, and in the word Morderor in ExodusExod. xxx. 23. alluding to Mordecai; again the sudden end of Haman is indicated in Joshua,Josh. v. 12. and his death on the gallows is hinted at in Genesis.Gen. iii. 11. Instead of the thorn (Haman) came up the fir-tree (Mordecai), and instead of the brier (Vashti) came up the myrtle tree (Esther.)See Talmud Megillah, x. HeAhasuerus. who listened to lying words, and who had already issued a hostile decree,Ezra iv. 6. touching the building of the
temple, presumed to invest himself in the priestly garments he had seized in Jerusalem,Megillah, xi. 2. having miscalculated the time fixed for the duration of the Babylonish captivity. According to his edict, diverse vessels from the marble temple of Solomon were used at the banquet, and Satan came also among them.The following is an allegory taken from the Medrash Rabbi in commenting upon the verse, Esth. ix. 1. And when the Israelites in Susan partook of the repast so fatal to them, he opened his mouth to slander them, and to deliver them up to Haman, who set a price on them, and the Almighty consented to write their sentence of destruction; when he said, “I will scatter them into corners. I will make the remembrance of them to cease from among men.” Then the holy angels cried bitterly, exclaiming, Merciful One, look on the covenant, and break it not utterly. The holy law which was given us as an inheritance heard it, and put on mourning and widow’s garments; she wrung her hands over her head, and walked forth crying. Elijah the Tishbite girt himself with sackcloth about his loins, instead of his girdle of leather, and speedily informed the three patriarchs, who sleep in the cave of Machpelah; then hastened to the former shepherd of the people, to Moses, saying, What meanest thou, O sleeper? Arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us! Then he revealed to Mordecai,After his conference with Moses. who was also called Bilshan, that the edict was sealed only with clay;And might, therefore, be revoked by prayer. and from the instance of Nineveh, too, they learned how to avert a sentence even after its being pronounced. So Mordecai, the son of Kish, knocked at the gates of the colleges, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat down on ashes. For three days he made the children suffer hunger and thirst, to weaken, by the voice of Jacob, the power of the insolent, and with outspread hands he prayed, “O Lord, save me from ignominy, and let not the enemy come and slay mother and child!” On both sides stood the children of the patriarchs and their teachers; they all cried, and their cries went up to the Lord. And when the prayer came before him, the Lord asked his attendants, “What voice, as the voice of lambs, is that in mine ears?” “They are,” replied the faithful shepherd (Moses), “the little ones of the sacred tribe. O Lord, deliver from this wicked enemy those who are doomed to die.” And the Gracious One was moved to compassion by the deplorable event, and when the King of Israel re-read in the book-
of fate the sentence of destruction, he tore it to pieces.Thus far the legend taken from מדרש רבה ותרגום שני Then Mordecai, the Jew, ordered Haman and his sons to be hanged on the tree, the children below and the father above, each occupying three yards, and a fourth was left between.In allusion to the gallows of 50 feet in height which Haman had erected for Mordecai. The father and the ten sons occupied a space of 33 yards; 10 interstices each of one yard amount to a total of 43 yards, consequently the lowest hung still seven yards above ground. (See תרגום שני פסוק ויתלו) He who was the second in the kingdom saw the vengeance, and in his joy poured forth his thanksgiving. Thus the Lord restored me again to mine office, and the arch enemy was hanged. And Esther described the miracle, that it might annually be read, like the thanksgiving of Hallel; and in heaven was ratified what below was joyfully accepted.i.e., the celebration of the festival by mutual presents and by alms-giving. May the Lord renew such wonders as those we testify to now; yea, at this time let enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews.
